name: Piquet
summary: Two-player trick-taking game with a 32-card deck, played as a six-hand match with discarding and declaration phases.
rules_text: Played with 32 cards (7-A). A partie is 6 deals. Deal 12 cards to each, 8 cards form the talon (5 + 3). Elder (non-dealer) must discard at least 1 up to 5, drawing same number from talon, then Younger discards at least 1 up to remaining cards. Players may declare carte blanche (no face cards) for 10 points. Then declaration: Point - longest suit length wins, tie broken by sum of values (A=11, face=10). Sequence - longest run of 3+ in one suit wins. Set - three or four of a kind of 10+ (three =3 pts, four=14/15). Elder states claim, Younger says Good/Not Good/Equal or asks for tie-breaker. Winning point scores its length, sequences score by table, sets score 3 or 14. After declarations, 12 tricks are played, elder leads. Must follow suit, highest card of led suit wins trick. 1 point per trick led before scoring? 1 per trick taken, 10 for most tricks, extra points for winning all tricks.
